airspace.name: Ukraine
airspace.source: Closed to civil flights since Russia's invasion; EASA CZIB-2022-01

airspace.name: Russia
airspace.source: Russia bars the airlines of the EU, the UK, the US, Canada and about 30 more countries; Japanese airlines have kept out since 2022. EASA CZIB 2025-01

airspace.name: Belarus
airspace.source: EU and UK airlines told to keep out since 2021

airspace.name: Pakistan, for Indian airlines
airspace.source: Pakistan's NOTAMs, renewed monthly since April 2025 (A0521/26 runs to 24 October 2026)

airspace.name: Iran
airspace.source: Open on paper since mid-2026 (the east only), but avoided by almost every foreign airline since the strikes of February 2026; EASA CZIB-2026-04, the FAA's prohibition

airspace.name: Conflict zones
airspace.source: EASA conflict zone bulletins that advise against all altitudes: Iraq (CZIB-2026-05), Lebanon (-06), Sudan (CZIB-2023-01), Yemen over land (CZIB-2017-07); France's and Italy's notices for Iraq. Afghanistan, Syria, Libya, Mali and Somalia aren't avoided: their warnings now cover only flights below FL260-FL320, and airliners cross them above it

airspace.name: North Korea
airspace.source: Avoided by foreign airlines since its missile tests over the Sea of Japan

airspace.name: The Tibetan Plateau
airspace.source: The Tibetan Plateau, Karakoram and Pamirs: if a cabin lost pressure there, there'd be no lower ground to descend to, so airliners keep to the few routes over it they're equipped for

airport_notes.KRT: Closed by the war in April 2023. Domestic flights resumed in February 2026, and a few international ones from April (Sudanair to Cairo, Badr Airlines to Istanbul); Port Sudan is still Sudan's main gateway.
